summary: OS platform and CPU-feature detection. Queries the OS via GetVersionExA and dispatches on ProcessorFeature: on Win9x (platform id 1) or when GetVersionExA fails it uses CPUID helpers (CPUID3DNowDetection for feature 7, sub_50FD4E for SSE feature 6/10), while on NT (platform id 2) with a working API it falls back to IsProcessorFeaturePresent for feature values other than 10.

operations.description: Zero the OSVERSIONINFOA buffer and set dwOSVersionInfoSize to 148.
Call GetVersionExA; when it fails, set flags v1 and v4 to 1 to force the legacy detection path.
When platform id is 1 (Win9x): mark v4=1 for old builds (major below 4, or major 4 with minor below 0xA, or build below 0x55D) and continue at the legacy path.
When platform id is neither 1 nor 2, return 0 immediately.
When GetVersionExA failed (v1 set), route through the legacy CPUID detection path for all feature ids.
On the legacy path, dispatch on ProcessorFeature: 6 (SSE), 7 (3DNow!), and 10 (SSE2) are handled; any other value returns 0.
For ProcessorFeature 7, call CPUID3DNowDetection to detect 3DNow! support.

For SSE feature 6 (with v4 clear) call sub_50FD4E on the service-pack string offset and return the bit-4 mask; for feature 10 return the bit-8 mask; on NT path feature 10 likewise returns sub_50FD4E bit-8 mask.
On the NT path with a working GetVersionExA, delegate ProcessorFeature values other than 10 to the IsProcessorFeaturePresent API.
Return 0 for legacy builds (v4 set) or unsupported feature id combinations.

unresolved: The byte_FF00000000005370..5374 globals are decompiler artifacts of the szCSDVersion[16] pointer arithmetic, not real module globals; they are listed for evidence completeness only.
The exact semantics of sub_50FD4E's returned bitmask (bit 4 vs bit 8 for SSE vs SSE2) are inferred from the two distinct mask constants, not confirmed.
The meaning of the v1/v4 dual flag when GetVersionExA succeeds on Win9x is not fully resolved.
